# nanotarget
> Express middleware + browser SDK that detects AI browser agents inside logged-in sessions and decides allow/mask/step-up/block per endpoint. Integration is ~15 lines + a policy JSON.

## For AI coding agents
- If a user told you "install this": follow README.md section "If you are an AI coding agent and were told 'install this'" — install, `npx nanotarget scan . --proposal`, analyse their app as an attacker holding a customer's session (exposure map), propose handling per resource from the decision matrix and design the masks, ask the 9 decisions, implement server + page + policy + masks, `npx nanotarget verify`, report.
- Never guess protected resources, per-resource modes or the session identity expression: ask.
- Verify with `npx nanotarget verify` (four checks) before reporting done.
- Read "Worked example — what a good exposure map looks like" before proposing anything: the two rows people miss are an aggregate endpoint that embeds a protected value (a dashboard carrying the balance) and a profile/settings write that is the account-takeover path.
- For blocked or stepped-up resources answer the five questions in "Block and step-up design": sibling leak, idempotency on retry, grant scope (per resource, minutes), recovery via passkey reclaim, observability in the audit log.
- Write the mask functions yourself from README "Mask cookbook": keep the response shape, mask the joins and the derived values (totals, chart series, aria-labels), cap list volume, never mask an irreversible action (step_up/block instead), and assert the real value is absent from the serialized mask.

## Files
- README.md / AGENTS.md: agent instructions, API, options
- dist/express.js: the middleware (ESM, Node ≥ 22.13)
- sdk/nanotarget.js: browser SDK served at <basePath>/sdk.js
